title: Sunan Ibn Majah
author: Ibn Majah (Abu ‘Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Qazwini)
edition_analyzed: Standard Arabic text with common English translations
target_audience: Muslim scholars (Ulama) and students of Islamic sciences
General Muslim audience seeking religious knowledge
Researchers of Islamic history and jurisprudence (fiqh)
Non-Muslims interested in primary Islamic texts
core_themes: Preservation and transmission of the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
Guidance on Islamic law, ethics, rituals, and daily life
Organization of religious, social, and personal conduct
Comprehensive understanding of Islamic beliefs and practices
primary_purpose: To compile and authenticate the sayings, actions, and approvals of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for the guidance of the Muslim community, and to serve as a key source of Islamic law and moral conduct.

structure_format.narrative_style: Formal, chain-of-narrators (isnad) followed by concise hadith texts (matn)
structure_format.organization: Arranged by topical books and chapters (Kitab, Bab); each entry comprises the chain of narrators and the hadith itself
features: Thematic grouping (e.g., purification, prayer, fasting, commerce, etiquette)
Occasional commentary and grading by later scholars on authenticity

key_concepts_lessons: The centrality of the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition) in Islamic law and life
Practical application of Islamic duties: prayer, fasting, charity, pilgrimage, marriage, business, and more
Norms of good character, manners, and interpersonal dealings
Criteria for evaluating and transmitting authentic traditions
Role of hadith in shaping faith, law, and community ethics
notable_features: Sixth and final book of the famous Kutub al-Sittah (the Six Major Hadith Collections in Sunni Islam)
Contains approximately 4340 hadith (by standard numbering), not all deemed authentic—some weak (da'if)
Particularly valued for unique narrations not found in other canonical collections
Widely used by jurists, preachers, and students, especially in conjunction with other major hadith works
Many hadith graded and analyzed by later scholars
cultural_historical_context: Compiled in the 9th century CE in the Abbasid era, part of the systematization of Islamic knowledge following centuries of oral transmission; Ibn Majah, a Persian hadith scholar from Qazvin, traveled widely and collected traditions to preserve Islamic teachings for future generations. Sunan Ibn Majah has a unique status among Sunni Muslims and is recognized as one of the six major canonical hadith collections, influencing Islamic law and practice.
reception_impact: Essential source for Sunni Islamic jurisprudence, exegesis, and teaching
Heavily referenced by scholars, though some questioned the authenticity of a portion of its hadith
Completes the six canonical books; its inclusion in the Kutub al-Sittah was later and sometimes debated but now widely standardized
Respected for its preservation of rare and unique prophetic traditions
Studied globally in Islamic seminaries (madrasas) and universities
